2	name: horizon-inbox
3	description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
4	---
5	
6	The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
7	future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
8	by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
9	fields.
10	
11	## Read
12	
13	- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
14	  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
15	  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
16	  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
17	  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
18	- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
19	  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
20	  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
21	  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
22	- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
23	  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
24	- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
25	  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
26	  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
27	  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
28	  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
29	- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
30	  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
31	  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
32	  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
33	  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
34	  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
35	- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
36	  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
37	  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
38	  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
39	  Scope/project says what the item is about.
40	- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
41	  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
42	  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
43	- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
44	  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
45	  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
46	  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
47	- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
48	  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
49	  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
50	  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
51	  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
52	  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).
53	
54	## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)
55	
56	Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
57	lightweight overlays keep it navigable:
58	
59	- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
60	  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
61	  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
62	  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
63	  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
64	  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
65	  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
66	- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
67	  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
68	  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
69	  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
70	  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
71	  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.
72	
73	Read in this order before editing:
74	
75	1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
76	   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
77	2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
78	   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
79	   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
80	3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.
81	
82	The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
83	it explicitly.
84	
85	## Act
86	
87	Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
88	attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
89	**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
90	`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
91	If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
92	work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
93	next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
94	comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
95	UI); you do not pass this yourself.
96	
97	New inbox items use a two-part body:
98	
99	- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
100	  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
101	- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
102	  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
103	  item that is only a title is rejected.
104	
105	Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Operational
106	messages are deltas, not reports. Default to one sentence or at most three short
107	bullets covering conclusion, new evidence, and next action; do not repeat the
108	thread, commit diff, or session history. Use headings only when a genuinely
109	multi-part decision needs them. Agent comments target at most 600 characters and
110	are rejected above 1200; descriptions/opening messages target 800 and are
111	rejected above 2400. Humans are not subject to these bounds.
112	
113	Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
114	`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
115	of that paragraph concise.
116	
117	Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
118	`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
119	`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
120	open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
121	main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
122	solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
123	obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.
124	
125	### Conversation lifecycle
126	
127	A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
128	one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.
129	
130	1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
131	   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
132	   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
133	   open one thread per incremental finding.
134	2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
135	   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
136	   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
137	3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
138	   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
139	   team.
140	4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
141	   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
142	   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
143	   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
144	   warning says the inbox is full.
145	5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
146	   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave
147	   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates
148	   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
149	   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.
150	6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations
151	   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real
152	   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is
153	   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.
154	
155	- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
156	  what changed; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
157	  into the body; authorship is automatic. Comment only at a **key advance** such
158	  as a milestone, ruled-out route, blocker, correction, or conclusion. Update the
159	  existing thread with the delta instead of re-establishing its full context.
160	- `horizon inbox dm task:<id> [task:<id> ...] --body "Topic\n\nOpening message"`
161	  — start a one-to-one or group conversation. Use `horizon ps` to discover live
162	  teams. Use it only after the lifecycle search above. The sender remains a
163	  participant and owns closure; every reply makes the thread unread for the other
164	  participants. Humans read and reply from the live dashboard.
165	- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
166	  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
167	  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
168	  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
169	  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
170	  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
171	  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
172	- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
173	  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
174	  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
175	  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.
176	  For a conversation you initiated, this is the normal "discussion finished"
177	  operation after its answer/conclusion has been consumed.
178	- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work
179	  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before
180	  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical
181	  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise
182	  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should
183	  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.
184	- `horizon inbox add --body "Short title\n\nDescription with details and next action." [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`
185	  — open a new item.
186	  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, `project:<name>`, or a direct
187	    message to another team `task:<id>` / `run:<id>`.
188	    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. "I rewrote your
189	    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it"); use `--to task:<id>` to
190	    message a specific running team.
191	  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of
192	    the shared default.
193	  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
194	  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`
195	    tag to the body.
196	  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
197	    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.
198	- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable
199	  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the "Memory"
200	  section and a human can prune it like any other item.
201	- `horizon inbox protect --body "..." [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`
202	  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),
203	  e.g. "do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`". These render as a
204	  "Protected" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that
205	  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed
206	  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.
207	
208	Reading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect
209	it every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is
210	one-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the "Protected" section are never
211	modified.
